additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional disorder is characterized by one or more persistent delusions lasting at least a month (often many months or years) in the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thought, or marked negative symptoms, and with relatively preserved overall functioning outside the delusional themes. The delusions are fixed false beliefs that remain resistant to clear contradictory evidence and are not better explained by mood episodes, substance use, or another psychotic disorder. Content can involve persecution, jealousy, somatic concerns, grandiosity, or erotomanic ideas, and behavior may be subtly shaped by these beliefs while still appearing outwardly organized. Onset is often insidious in mid to later adulthood, and patients frequently present only after family, employers, or legal systems become involved because the person does not recognize the beliefs as pathological.

patient.stressor: Allen’s problems became noticeable after he developed chronic shoulder pain that limited his welding work and kept him from his usual fishing and woodworking, leaving him spending long evenings alone in his workshop and online. Following a routine imaging study that showed only mild degenerative changes, he became convinced that the clinic had concealed a serious implant or device placed in his body without consent, and he began poring over technical manuals and internet forums to "prove" it. Over the next nine months, his belief hardened despite repeated reassurances from different physicians, leading him to refuse recommended physical therapy, cancel a planned Canadian fishing trip, and start modifying metal tools and building contraptions in his shed to "detect" the supposed device. After he angrily demanded that a local surgeon remove the non‑existent implant and threatened to expose a "cover‑up" at the hospital, his wife—worried about his escalating preoccupation and withdrawal from family life—insisted he see a psychiatrist before any further medical appointments.
patient.chief_complaint: “The doctors keep telling me nothing is there, but I know they put something inside me and they’re hiding it.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Ever since that shoulder scan, I’m dead sure they slipped some kind of tracking or testing gadget into me without saying a word, and no matter how many doctors or my wife tell me I’m being ridiculous, I can feel it in there and I’ve spent night after night in my shop reading manuals and building metal rigs to try to catch a signal or reading between the lines of my medical records, because I know the hospital and maybe even the government are in on keeping this thing quiet.

add_requirements.functioning_not_markedly_impaired_apart_: Aside from all the time I spend trying to prove they put something in my shoulder, I still get up for my shifts, handle the bills with my wife, and can talk to people at work about normal stuff like sports and the weather without any trouble.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve turned down extra hours and stopped going on fishing trips or family get‑togethers because I feel like I have to stay home working on these detection rigs and arguing with doctors about this implant instead.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about nine months now, ever since that first shoulder scan when I became convinced they hid something inside me.
